questions.stem: Metallic conductors and semiconductors are heated separately. What are the changes with respect to conductivity?
questions.solution:
For Metallic Conductors, $R \propto T$ (R is the resistance)
Hence conductivity decreases with increase of Temperature
For semi-conductors, conductivity increases with rise of temperature due increase in number of electron-hole pairs.

questions.stem:
The equivalent weight of $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}$(Gram molecular weight = M) in the given reaction is
$\mathrm{I_2 + 2Na_2S_2O_3 = 2\,NaI + Na_2S_4O_6}$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{I_2 + 2Na_2\overset{+2}{S_2}O_3 = 2NaI + Na_2\overset{+2.5}{S_4}O_6}$
$n\cdot f = 2 \times 0.5 = 1$
$\therefore$ Number of moles of electron lost per mole of $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3}$ = 1
Hence equivalent weight of $\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3} = \frac{M}{1} = M$

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is correct for a spontaneous polymerization reaction ?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{nA \rightarrow A_n}$
During spontaneous polymerisation reaction number of particles decreases, hence entropy decreases.
Being spontaneous $\Delta G$ of the reaction is less than zero.
$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$
To make the $\Delta G$ negative, $\Delta H$ must be negative i.e. less than zero.

questions.stem: The compressibility factor for a van der Waal gas at high pressure is
questions.solution:
For 1 mol van der Waal’s gas
$\left(P + \frac{a}{V^{2}}\right)(v - b) = RT$
At high pressure $P + \frac{a}{V^{2}} \approx P$
$\therefore P(V - b) = RT$
$\therefore PV - Pb = RT$
$PV = RT + Pb$
$z = \frac{PV}{RT} = \frac{RT}{RT} + \frac{Pb}{RT}$
$\therefore z = 1 + \frac{Pb}{RT}$

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is true about equilibrium constant and rate constant of a single step chemical reaction?
questions.solution:
According to Van’t Hoff equation
$\log\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \frac{\Delta H}{2.303R}\left[\frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2}\right]$
Where $k_1$ and $k_2$ are Equilibrium Constants at $T_1$ and $T_2$ temperature respectively.
When $\Delta H > 0$ (Endothermic process)
then Equilibrium Constant increases with increase in temperature
When $\Delta H < 0$ (Exothermic process)
then Equilibrium Constant decreases with increases in temperature.
According to Arrhenius equation
$\log\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \frac{E_a}{2.303R}\left[\frac{1}{T_1} - \frac{1}{T_2}\right]$
where $k_1$ and $k_2$ are Rate Constants at $T_1$ and $T_2$ temperature respectively.
$E_a$ (Activation energy) > 0
When temperature increases rate constant will increase

options.text: Equilibrium constant may increase or decrease but rate constant always increases with temperature
Both equilibrium constant and rate constant increase with temperature
Rate constant may increase or decrease but equilibrium constant always increases with temperature
Both equilibrium constant and rate constant decrease with temperature

questions.stem: Which hydrogen like species will have the same radius as that of 1st Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom?
questions.solution:
Radius of nth orbit $= 0.529\,\frac{n^{2}}{Z}$ Å
Radius of 1st Bohr Orbit of Hydrogen atom $= 0.529 \times \frac{1^{2}}{1} = 0.529$ Å
Radius of 2nd Bohr Orbit of $\mathrm{Be^{3+}}$ $= 0.529\,\frac{2^{2}}{4} = 0.529$ Å

questions.stem: Equal volumes of aqueous solution of 0.1(M) HCl and 0.2 (M) $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ are mixed. The concentration of $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ions in the resulting solution is
questions.solution:
Concentration of $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ in molarity $= \frac{\text{Total no. of mole of H}^{+}}{\text{Total volume of solution (in L)}} = \frac{\sum M \times V(\text{in L}) \times \text{Basicity}}{\sum V}$
$= \frac{V \times 0.1 \times 1 + V \times 0.2 \times 2}{V + V} = \frac{0.5}{2} = 0.25$ M

questions.stem:
What will be the change in acidity if
(i) $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ is added in saturated $\mathrm{(NH_4)_2SO_4}$ solution
(ii) $\mathrm{SbF_5}$ is added in anhydrous HF
questions.solution:
i) $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}_{(aq)} + 4NH^{+}_{4\,(aq)} \rightarrow [Cu(NH_3)_4]^{+2} + 4H^{+}_{(aq)}}$
Formation of stable $\mathrm{[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{+2}}$ complex increases $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ion concentration, thus acidity increases
ii) $\mathrm{HF + HF \rightleftharpoons H_2F^{+} + F^{-}}$
$\mathrm{SbF_5}$ removes $\mathrm{F^{-}}$ as $\mathrm{SbF_6^{-}}$ and shifts equilibrium forward to increase $\mathrm{H_2F^{+}}$

questions.stem: pH of $10^{-8}$ (M) HCI solution is
questions.solution:
For $10^{-8}$(M) HCI solution, the solution being very dilute, $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ion conc. is not significant as compared to $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ion furnished from $\mathrm{H_2O}$.
thus, $\mathrm{H^{+}_{total} = H^{+}_{HCl} + H^{+}_{H_2O}}$
$= 10^{-8} + 10^{-7}$ (approx)
$= 1.1 \times 10^{-7}$ (approx)
$\mathrm{pH} = -\log(1.1 \times 10^{-7})$
$= 7 - \log(1.1) = 6.96$ (approx)
$\therefore$ Value of pH is greater than 6, less than 7.

questions.stem: The specific conductance (k) of 0.02 (M) aqueous acetic acid solution at 298K is $1.65 \times 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{S\,cm^{-1}}$. The degree of dissociation of acetic acid is $[\lambda^{\circ}_{\mathrm{H^{+}}} = 349.1\ \mathrm{S\,cm^{2}\,mol^{-1}}$ and $\lambda^{\circ}_{\mathrm{CH_3COO^{-}}} = 40.9\ \mathrm{S\,cm^{2}\,mol^{-1}}]$
questions.solution:
Firstly we find $\lambda_m$ (aq $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$)
$\lambda_m = \frac{K \times 1000}{C(M)} = \frac{1.65 \times 10^{-4} \times 1000}{0.02} = 8.25\ \mathrm{S\,cm^{2}\,mol^{-1}}$
$\lambda_m$ ($\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ at infinite dilution) $= \lambda^{\infty}_{m}(\mathrm{H^{+}}) + \lambda^{\infty}_{m}(\mathrm{CH_3COO^{-}})$
Now degree of dissociation
$\alpha = \frac{\lambda_m[\mathrm{CH_3COOH\ at\ 0.02(M)}]}{\lambda_m[\mathrm{CH_3COOH\ at\ infinite\ dilution}]}$
$\alpha = \frac{8.25}{349.1 + 40.9} = 0.021$

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about the $S_N2$ reaction mechanism is/are true ?
questions.solution: $S_N2$ reaction rate depends upon the nucleophilicity of the attacking nueleophile. Here the 2 in the notation stands for Bimolecularity. Tert-butyl substrate fails in $S_N2$ due to crowding. Optical rotation does not change necessarily from (+) to (–) or (–) to (+), as the product is not necessarily an isomer of reactant.

options.text: The rate of reaction increases with increasing nucleophilicity.
The number 2 denotes a second order reaction
Tertiary butyl substrates do not follow this mechanism
The optical rotation of substrates always changes from (+) to (–) or from (–) to (+) in the products

questions.stem: Which of the following represent(s) the enantiomer of Y ?
questions.solution:

questions.stem: Which of the following ion/ions is/are diamagnetic ?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ is a $d^{6}$ ion. With strong field ligand like $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$ has no unpaired electron. For $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$, $\mathrm{F^{-}}$ is a weak field ligand.
$\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ is a $d^{6}$ ion. With strong field ligand $\mathrm{CN^{-}}$, $\mathrm{[Fe(CN)_6]^{4-}}$ has no unpaired electron. For $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$ is a weak field ligand.
